case_name: T. C. Pathak v State of Uttar Pradesh and Others
facts: The grievance of the petitioner, T. C. Pathak, is that his son Nirdesh Pathak alias Neetu was forcibly taken away by Respondents 4 and 5 and some constables from his shop on 25-8-1994 at about 10.00 a.m. and that his whereabouts are not known.
After a notice was issued on the said writ petition to Respondents 3, 4 and 5, Nirdesh Pathak alias Neetu was presented in the court on 19-9-1994.

Nirdesh Pathak was brought by Sub-Inspector, Sukrant Sharma (Respondent 5), Constable 1195 Mange Ram, Constable 1175 Anil and Constable 749 Balister to Police Station Jehangirabad, District Bulandshahr, though the records of the police station concerned do not disclose the bringing or purpose of bringing aforesaid Nirdesh Pathak @ Neetu to the police station.
It is further stated that the enquiry has also revealed that the aforesaid Nirdesh Pathak @ Neetu was kept at the police station from 25-8-1994 to 28-8-1994.

Respondent 4, Rombir Singh, and Respondent 5, Sukrant Sharma, have filed affidavits wherein they have disputed the correctness of the averments contained in the counter-affidavit filed by Shri K. L. Meena
Nirdesh Pathak @ Neetu was produced in the court on 19-9-1994, and he is now free.
The prayer for the relief of writ of habeas corpus no longer survives.
petitioner_arguments: The grievance of the petitioner, T. C. Pathak, is that his son Nirdesh Pathak alias Neetu was forcibly taken away by Respondents 4 and 5 and some constables from his shop on 25-8-1994 at about 10.00 a.m. and that his whereabouts are not known.
respondent_arguments: Respondent 4, Rombir Singh, and Respondent 5, Sukrant Sharma, have filed affidavits wherein they have disputed the correctness of the averments contained in the counter-affidavit filed by Shri K. L. Meena
court_reasoning: This shows that there has been denial of the right of Nirdesh Pathak @ Neetu to personal liberty guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution on account of his illegal confinement in the police station and his being subjected to torture while in such confinement.

We are, however, of the opinion that the counter-affidavit filed by Shri K. L. Meena indicates that Nirdesh Pathak @ Neetu was kept in illegal confinement in Police Station, Jehangirabad during the period from 25-8-1994 to 28-8-1994 and was also tortured while thus confined in the police station.
We are of the view that he should be suitably compensated for this denial of his constitutional right.
holding: The State of U.P. to pay a sum of Rs. 10,000 to Nirdesh Pathak @ Neetu by way of compensation for the denial of his constitutional right under Article 21 of the Constitution.
The said payment should be made within a period of one month.
cases_cited: T. C. Pathak v State of Uttar Pradesh
